h: Getting the Most From a Visit to the Cats
p: Because visits here are so carefully managed, a little preparation goes a long way. Read the details of your chosen experience before you book, as each one is designed for different ages and interests, and some may have minimum age limits. If you're buying it as a gift, it's worth checking what dates are available first so the lucky person isn't left waiting ages for a slot.

Bring the right kit. A camera with a decent zoom lens will be your best friend, as the cats are in spacious enclosures and won't always pose by the fence. Binoculars are handy too. Dress for being outdoors in the Kent countryside, with waterproofs and sturdy footwear, because the paths can get muddy after rain.

Most of all, go with the right mindset. This isn't a place where animals perform on cue. Big cats can be shy and spend a lot of the day resting, so a sighting of a leopard slinking through the long grass feels all the more special. Listen closely to the keepers too, because the stories of individual cats, where they came from and how they're cared for, are what make a visit here so memorable.

Smarden sits in the heart of the Kent Weald, a gorgeous patch of countryside full of half-timbered villages, oast houses and orchards. Sissinghurst Castle Garden, the famous National Trust garden created by Vita Sackville-West, is only a few miles away and makes a lovely pairing. Further afield, Leeds Castle near Maidstone is a classic Kentish day out, with its moat, grounds and maze, so you could easily build a whole countryside weekend around your big cat visit.
